precepts.text: He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel. He hath not dealt so with any nation. That law and light was only given to the Israelites.
precepts.point: The woman fled into the wilderness, where she hath a place prepared of God. The wilderness is Africa; we fled out of Jerusalem into Africa, the same place where Joseph took the young child and his mother. Then a place was prepared, which is the Americas. A thousand two hundred and threescore days: 1260 days, three and a half, the same period written as forty and two months and as a time, times, and the dividing of time in Daniel 7 and 8.

note.label: 250 Years of Celebration 400 Years of Sweat Equity (Pt 2)

precepts.why:
The woman is “clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet.” The Bible says the commandments are a lamp and the law is light. That is the sun and the moon it is talking about there, and that light was only given to the Israelites.

The psalm says so: “He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel. He hath not dealt so with any nation: and as for his judgments, they have not known them.”

God gave his word, his statutes and his judgments to Jacob and to Israel, and he has not dealt so with any other nation. That is why the woman is clothed with that light and no one else is. The woman crowned with twelve stars and clothed with the sun and moon is the nation that received the law: the twelve tribes of Israel.

precepts.text: The heart is the mind: the broken in heart are the broken in mind and spirit.
precepts.point: Missing a dollar-eighteen gas is wanting America to continue; the affliction has to happen, and when we see these things our salvation draws near.

note.label: Eleutherophobia the Fear of Freedom

precepts.why:
The psalm says the Lord “gathereth together the outcasts of Israel. He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds.” Who are the broken in heart? We are the ones broken in mind and spirit, because the heart is the mind. Christ shows it: “For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts”. Thoughts come out of the heart, so the heart is the mind.

The broken in heart are the broken in mind: the twelve tribes, the outcasts of Israel. And it is the Lord who “bindeth up their wounds”. Everything we went through in captivity, it is the Lord that will minister the ointment to fix and heal his nation. These other nations cannot fix you with their philosophies and doctrines; they don't care about us and do not want to restore us, because restoring us means giving back everything they spoiled from the children of Israel.

Many of our brothers and sisters feel the only way we will come together is by the hands of these other nations. But it is Christ who is coming to restore this glorious nation, build up Jerusalem, gather the outcasts, and heal the broken in mind.

precepts.text: He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel; he hath not dealt so with any nation. The commandments were given to the twelve tribes, and Israel is the nation that gets judged. That is why our people went into the trans-Saharan and trans-Atlantic slave trades.
precepts.point: The whole head is sick. You are sick and I am sick. That is the whole point of the class: we have to keep getting right.

note.label: Wars Are Here: Seek Good Not Evil

precepts.why:
Isaiah says the sinful nation has “provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger”. To prove which nation that is: “He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel.” Jacob was the forefather of the twelve tribes, and his name later became Israel. The statutes and the judgments were given to the nation of Israel.

“He hath not dealt so with any nation”. So for modern-day Christians to say that God is dealing with all nations and all people, they don't know the Bible.

Then: “and as for his judgments, they have not known them.” The Israelites are the ones that get judged. That is why Black people went into slavery, in the trans-Saharan slave trade and the trans-Atlantic slave trade, and many other times in history we have served our enemies in slavery.

So Isaiah was never talking about anybody but the Israelites. We are the seed of evildoers who call evil good and good evil, led astray by Christian pastors and the leaders in the mosques. From 1865 to 1965 we lived under more overt racism, but we had civility, women had a dress code, and there was an order to talk to a sister. Since 1965 we have gained almost twenty million abortions by Black women alone and the dumbest generation of children with the smartest technology. We provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, and that is why we went into slavery.

precepts.point: And that will by no means clear the guilty: He will forgive you, but you will still be judged; He still visits the iniquity of the fathers upon the children and upon the children's children, unto the third and to the fourth generation.

note.label: Exodus 34: The Second Tables and the Covenant Renewed

precepts.why:
“Keeping mercy for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin”: this is spoken to Israel. “He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel. He hath not dealt so with any nation: and as for his judgments, they have not known them.”

Moses is speaking only to the children of Israel at this time. The word and the statutes were given to Israel only, so the forgiveness proclaimed on the mount belongs to Israel.

precepts.text: He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel; he hath not dealt so with any nation. Keep this precept under your belt, it is brought out almost every camp.
precepts.point: The whole book of Deuteronomy is the Lord speaking unto his people Israel; he showed his statutes and his judgments to no other nation.

note.label: Deuteronomy 12: The Place Where the Lord Puts His Name

precepts.why:
“He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel. He hath not dealt so with any nation: and as for his judgments, they have not known them. Praise ye the Lord.” The statutes and judgments Moses sets out here, “which ye shall observe to do in the land”, were shown to Jacob and to Israel, and to no other nation. The whole book of Deuteronomy is the Lord speaking unto his people Israel.

The land itself was given to the fathers while other nations were living in it, and Israel went to war with those nations to take it; the statutes and judgments belong to Israel in that land, “all the days that ye live upon the earth.” The other nations have not known his judgments; he has not dealt so with any of them. Keep Psalms 147:19-20 under your belt: it is brought out almost every camp.

precepts.text: He showed His word unto Jacob and His judgments unto Israel; He has not dealt so with any nation.
precepts.point: The heathen having "not known thee" does not mean there are heathen who do know the Lord. To know God is to keep His commandments, and the commandments were only given to the israelites. The other nations do not truly know God, His ways, or His judgments; we do.

note.label: Psalm 79: The Heathen Have Defiled Thy Inheritance

precepts.why:
The prayer asks the Most High to “Pour out thy wrath upon the heathen that have not known thee, and upon the kingdoms that have not called upon thy name.” The heathen having not known thee does not mean there are heathen who do know the Lord.

Psalm 147 settles it: “He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel. He hath not dealt so with any nation: and as for his judgments, they have not known them. Praise ye the Lord.” He showed his word unto Jacob and his judgments unto Israel; he has not dealt so with any nation.

To know God is to keep his commandments, and the commandments were only given to the israelites. The other nations do not truly know God, his ways or his judgments; we do. So the wrath poured out on the heathen that have not known him is wrath on those who “devoured Jacob, and laid waste his dwelling place”, the nations who were never given his judgments.

precepts.text: He shows His word and statutes to Jacob and Israel; He has not dealt so with any other nation.
precepts.point: When Israel fled Egypt there were oppressed nations who came out with us; the Bible calls them strangers. But the ways of the Most High were made known to Moses and Israel.

note.label: Psalm 103: Bless the Lord for His Benefits to Israel

precepts.why:
“He made known his ways unto Moses, his acts unto the children of Israel.” Look at that: his acts unto the children of Israel, not to every nation.

David says the same later: “He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel. He hath not dealt so with any nation: and as for his judgments, they have not known them. Praise ye the Lord.” He shows his word and his statutes to Jacob and Israel; he has not dealt so with any other nation, and the other nations have not known his judgments.

When Israel fled Egypt there were oppressed nations who came out with us; the Bible calls them strangers. But the ways of the Most High were made known to Moses and Israel, and no other nation was dealt with so.

precepts.text: The Most High sets His hand the second time to recover the remnant of His people from Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar, Hamath, and the islands of the sea, assembling the outcasts of Israel and the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
precepts.point: In church they talk a lot about the outcasts of Israel being Gentiles and things of that nature, but this shows plainly that Israel are the people being gathered. Our people are going to be gathered from many different places, from the four corners of the earth, from Assyria, Hamath, Egypt, and Cush. Our people are in Israel, in India, in Arabia, and all over the world.

note.label: Psalm 147: The Most High Gathers the Outcasts of Israel

precepts.why:
“The Lord doth build up Jerusalem: he gathereth together the outcasts of Israel.” In church they talk a lot about the outcasts of Israel being Gentiles and things of that nature, but this shows plainly that Israel are the people being gathered: “the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea. And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.”

Our people are going to be gathered from many different places, from the four corners of the earth, from Assyria, Hamath, Egypt, and Cush. Our people are in Israel, in India, in Arabia, and all over the world.

note.label: Psalm 147: The Most High Gathers the Outcasts of Israel

“The Lord taketh pleasure in them that fear him, in those that hope in his mercy.” We are still talking about Israel here. “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endureth for ever.” Those that fear the Lord are those that do his commandments; the way we know what fear is comes through the precepts.

Those that hope in his mercy are going to keep his commandments. That is why faith without works is dead; you have to have faith and you have to have works. You hope in his mercy and you keep his commandments.

The Most High taketh pleasure in them that fear him, and we know what that fear is through the precepts. You hope in his mercy and you keep his commandments, because faith without works is dead.

note.label: Isaiah 43: Ye Are My Witnesses

precepts.why:
“Therefore I have profaned the princes of the sanctuary, and have given Jacob to the curse, and Israel to reproaches.” Why Jacob? “He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel. He hath not dealt so with any nation: and as for his judgments, they have not known them. Praise ye the Lord.”

The Most High showed his word, his statutes and his judgments unto Jacob and Israel; he has not dealt so with any nation, for no other nation knows the judgments of God. Because Israel alone was given the word, Israel alone is held to it: “thou hast made me to serve with thy sins, thou hast wearied me with thine iniquities”, “Thy first father hath sinned, and thy teachers have transgressed against me”, and so the Most High gave Jacob to the curse.
